subjects.label: Gore and dismemberment
subjects.description: Blood, severed heads and limbs, burning bodies and how graphic the violence is; the joke that the player has become a psychopath belongs in its own row.

subjects.label: Psychopath jokes and catharsis
subjects.description: The running joke that the game has made the player a murderer, from FBI watchlists and needing therapy to what grandma would think, together with using it to vent anger; the gore itself is not this row.

subjects.label: Physics and ragdolls
subjects.description: The physics-driven combat: how a blade lands, ragdolls that cling or flop, bodies reacting to a stab, and whether the physics feels right or awful; the weapons and spells themselves have their own rows.

subjects.label: Spells and telekinesis
subjects.description: Casting magic: telekinesis, summoned and thrown daggers, fire and gravity, and the game as a magic sandbox; steel weapons do not belong here.

subjects.label: Melee arsenal
subjects.description: The weapons themselves: swords, daggers, spears and shields and how many there are to pick up; how a hit behaves belongs in the physics row.

subjects.label: Enemies and NPC behaviour
subjects.description: The opponents: how they react when hit, fighting a group at once, enemy types such as golems and the ones players feel are missing; the player's own tools are not this row.

subjects.label: Sandbox versus campaign
subjects.description: The game as a goalless sandbox with no story, and the progression mode with lore and an ending that arrived later; how many hours it lasts in general stays in the content row.

subjects.label: Franchise roleplay
subjects.description: Playing as characters from other franchises, above all Star Wars with lightsabers and Jedi through mods such as the Outer Rim, plus Thanos and Batman; the game's own medieval setting is not this row.

subjects.label: Exertion and room knocks
subjects.description: Playing it as a workout that burns calories, and the bruises that come with it: hurt fingers, hitting a friend with the controller, and the walls of the room; motion sickness and tracking stay in the VR row.
